strategies.label: Synonymy
strategies.definition: A more common and general word is used instead of a more complex or specific one.
strategies.source_prompt: Select the complex or specific source expression.
strategies.simple_prompt: Select the simpler or more general replacement.

strategies.label: Modulation
strategies.definition: Information is redistributed or expressed linearly.
strategies.source_prompt: Select the source information whose organization changes.
strategies.simple_prompt: Select the corresponding information in its clearer or more linear organization.

strategies.label: Compression
strategies.definition: Grammatical or semantic constructs are compressed while their central content remains represented.
strategies.simple_prompt: Select the expression that preserves it in compressed form.

strategies.label: Explanation
strategies.definition: A word, expression, implicit grammatical construct, or implicit content is explained or made explicit using other words.
strategies.source_prompt: Select the source word, expression, or implicit-content anchor being explained.
strategies.simple_prompt: Select the words that provide the explanation or make the content explicit.

strategies.label: Syntactic Change
strategies.definition: A unit is changed into a different syntactic unit using the same words.
strategies.source_prompt: Select the source construction involved in the syntactic change.

strategies.label: Omission
strategies.definition: Material considered unnecessary for understanding an idea is removed.
strategies.source_prompt: Select the source material that was omitted.
strategies.simple_prompt: No simplified-side evidence is required unless useful for context.
